sentences.text: Mr. Satish Gupta, G. A. for the State.

Mr. V. R. Tiwari, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Vaibhav Shukla, Advocate and Ms. Astha Shukla,
Advocate for the respondents No. 2 and 3.
Ms. Anuja Sharma, Advocate appearing on behalf of Mr. Rama Kant Mishra, Dy. S. G. for Union of India.

The petitioners have approached this Court raising a grievance that their claims regarding the grant of appropriate compensation and rehabilitation--particularly the provision of employment--have not been duly considered by the respondents, namely, the South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL),
the State Government, and the Union of India Learned counsel for SECL has submitted that the petitioners are not entitled to employment or compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act).

sentences.text: Earlier vide order dated 18.04.2025, an order of status quo was granted in favour of petitioner by this Court.
Relevant portion of the said order is quoted below for ready reference : -

"Accordingly, as an interim measure, the respondent No. 2 & 3, the SECL is directed to refrain from undertaking any operations in the land of the petitioners and also in the vicinity of the petitioner's land.
There shall be status quo maintained by the parties with respect to excavation and all activities on and near the petitioner's land."
Considering the urgency and gravity of the matter, this Court deems it appropriate to modify the interim relief earlier granted vide order dated 18.04.2025.
It is hereby directed that SECL shall be permitted to carry out excavation activities on the lands legally acquired from the petitioners.
However, this permission shall not be construed as a license to extend excavation operations beyond the boundaries of the acquired land.
Under no circumstances the respondents shall encroach upon or conduct any excavation in areas that have not been lawfully acquired in accordance with applicable statutory provisions.
SECL is further directed to take necessary precautions regarding the explosion to ensure that the villagers are not affected in any way.

Learned counsel for the respective respondents are directed to file reply within three weeks and thereafter, two weeks more time is granted to learned counsel for the petitioner to file additional rejoinder to the reply, if any.

After the receipt of aforesaid pleadings, matter will be heard by this Court on the issue with respect to grant of compensation and rehabilitation to the petitioners under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act).
